name: How do I know if my guest bathroom is a refresh or a full remodel?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell whether my guest bathroom project is just a refresh or a true full remodel?
mainEntity.text: How can I tell whether my guest bathroom project is just a refresh or a true full remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The difference comes down to how much of the bathroom is being rebuilt. A refresh usually focuses on visible upgrades such as paint, vanity replacement, lighting, mirror, hardware, and maybe minor tile repairs. A full remodel goes much deeper and often includes demolition, waterproofing, new tile assemblies, plumbing or electrical changes, and possibly a revised layout. If the work involves opening walls, changing the shower or tub area, or addressing hidden damage, it is no longer just a refresh. This distinction is important because budget, schedule, and permit needs change quickly once the project moves from surface updates to system work. In many Los Angeles homes, homeowners start by wanting a refresh and then discover that old plumbing, poor ventilation, or water damage makes a fuller remodel the smarter choice. Defining the scope early helps set realistic expectations and avoid surprise costs.
acceptedAnswer.description: A refresh mainly changes visible finishes such as paint, vanity, mirror, fixtures, and limited tile. A full remodel usually includes demolition, waterproofing, plumbing or electrical updates, and possibly layout changes. If walls, floors, or wet areas are being rebuilt, it is a full remodel.
